processing: Orthodox high-grown Ceylon black tea, sold in grades such as BOP; part of it appears under the Lovers Leap mark.
harvest_season: Year-round, helped by the mix of rain and sun at this height; as with other Nuwara Eliya teas, the early months of the year are usually most prized.
appearance_dry: Small, fairly light-coloured dark leaf in the BOP grade, sometimes with greenish flecks, as is common at this altitude.
appearance_liquor: Pale, bright golden amber, typical of Nuwara Eliya.
appearance_wet: Light coppery leaf with some green.
taste_profile: Light and delicate, as Nuwara Eliya teas tend to be, with a clean brisk edge and a floral lift rather than weight.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western style. Skip the milk, and keep steeps short: this leaf turns sharp quickly.

vintage_note: Sold through the Colombo auction by grade, and to visitors as current production from the estate's own boutique, without a vintage. A delicate high-grown tea loses aroma early, so drink it within a year.
description:
Pedro is a high-grown estate near Nuwara Eliya town, at about 1,828 to 2,400 metres. Its seven divisions include Lovers' Leap, whose name also appears on some of its tea.

The cool, wet climate slows growth, which gives the light, delicate cup Nuwara Eliya is known for. It is made in the orthodox way, and its strength is fragrance and brightness rather than body.

Brew it gently, with water a little off the boil and a short steep. Milk will flatten it, and a long steep will turn it sharp rather than strong.

You can tour the factory and buy from the Lovers' Leap boutique above the plantation. Abroad, look for Pedro or Lovers Leap on single-estate packs, and go for recent lots.

The Lovers Leap name comes from a local legend about an eloping prince and the nearby waterfall, so treat it as a story and not as anything to do with the tea.
history:
One account gives 1840 for the estate, first growing coffee and cinchona and switching to tea in 1870, and has a first factory by 1880. Tourist pages often tie it to James Taylor, the pioneer of Ceylon tea, but those claims are loose; his own pioneering work was at Loolecondera in 1867.

The Nuwara Eliya Tea Company ran it from 1898 until nationalisation in 1972, and Kelani Valley Plantations has held it since 1992. In June 2022 a BOP under the Lovers Leap mark reached Rs. 2,200 per kilo at auction.
